title: Phrae-Nan 4-Day Road Trip Itinerary - Quiet Northern Thailand Drive | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: 4-day Phrae-Nan road trip: old-town Phrae, teak houses, indigo fabric, then Nan's Wat Phumin, Pua, Bo Kluea, and Sapan. Day-by-day schedule with real food stops and driving tips.
keywords: Phrae Nan trip, Phrae Nan itinerary, road trip Phrae Nan, Nan 4 days, driving northern Thailand
h1:
Phrae-Nan 4 Days 3 Nights
A Quiet Northern Road Trip
intro: Phrae and Nan are a natural pair -- connected by Highway 101, roughly 2 hours apart, and both built on the same quiet rhythm: old towns, teak houses, indigo cloth, ancient temples, and rice paddies cupped between mountains. If you want to slow down and actually look at things instead of ticking off Instagram spots, this route delivers. We've laid it out day by day -- times, real food stops, and places that are actually open right now.

blocks.html: If you have got four days off and want to go north without fighting for a parking spot, the Phrae-Nan corridor is the answer. Phrae is a town most people drive straight through on their way to Nan, but there is a full day of things here -- century-old teak mansions, indigo workshops in Ban Thung Hong, coffee in the old town. Nan itself is nature and culture running in parallel: Wat Phumin in the city centre, then paddy terraces and mountain villages out toward Pua, Bo Kluea, and Sapan. This itinerary starts in Phrae and works north, so the last days are spent with mountain views all around.

From Bangkok, driving to Phrae takes roughly 7-8 hours via Nakhon Sawan, Phitsanulok, and Uttaradit -- enter at Amphoe Den Chai, then turn onto Highway 101 into town. The Phrae-to-Nan leg runs entirely on 101, about 118 km, taking around 2 hours. The final stretch winds up into the hills but the road surface is good and not difficult to drive.

items: Own car -- By far the most practical option for this route. Many of Nan's highlights (Pua, Bo Kluea, Sapan) are outside town and public transport does not reach them conveniently.

Fly into Nan, rent a car -- Daily flights run Bangkok-Nan Nakhon Airport. If you do not want the long drive from Bangkok, fly in, rent a car at the airport, and run the itinerary in reverse from Nan down to Phrae.
Bus or van -- Coaches run from Bangkok to both Phrae and Nan. But once you arrive, you will still need to rent or hire a car to get around, especially for the mountain villages.

blocks.title: Before You Head Up
blocks.html: Fill up on petrol before the Pua-Bo Kluea-Sapan stretch -- stations are far apart and mobile signal drops out in places. Download offline maps before you leave.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Walking Phrae Old Town -- Teak Houses and Temples

items.activity: Arrive in Phrae, check into accommodation in town
items.note: Most places to stay sit around the old-town perimeter -- you can walk to the kum mansions and temples from here.

items.activity: Kum Chao Luang + Baan Wongburi
items.note: Baan Wongburi is a hundred-year-old pink teak house with intricate fretwork detailing. Entry is a few tens of baht -- wander through and see the belongings of Phrae's old ruling family.

items.activity: Wat Phra Baht Ming Mueang + stroll along Kham Lue Road
items.note: The old-town neighbourhood mixes aged timber shophouses with small cafes -- good for an easy wander and photos.

items.activity: Kad Kong Kao walking street (Saturday nights only)
items.note: Phrae's weekend market runs along Kham Lue Road near Kum Wongburi -- local food and handmade goods. If it is not Saturday, head out for khao soi or northern-style rice noodles in red pork broth around town instead.

blocks.html: Day one is about resting your legs after the drive and taking Phrae at a gentle pace. The town gets warm during the day but cools quickly, so the evening hours are when the atmosphere really comes alive. Do not miss khao khaep (Phrae's crispy rice crackers) and kao nom jeen nam ngiao -- the northern-style rice noodles in rich pork-tomato broth, sold around the morning market.

blocks.text: Day 2 -- Indigo Village, Then Up to Nan

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Phra That Cho Hae -- Indigo at Ban Thung Hong -- Drive to Nan

items.activity: Breakfast in town
items.note: Try khao khaep with nam ngiao, or coffee at one of the old teak shophouses.

items.activity: Wat Phra That Cho Hae
items.note: Phrae's most revered stupa -- the auspicious temple for those born in the Year of the Tiger, about 9 km outside town. Open 06:00-19:00.

items.activity: Ban Thung Hong -- indigo (mor hom) weaving village
items.note: Home of the classic Phrae mor hom indigo work shirt. Shops here let you watch the dyeing process and buy direct. Some run tie-dye workshops you can join.

items.activity: Lunch before heading out
Drive to Nan via Highway 101
items.note: About 118 km, roughly 2 hours. Plenty of mountain scenery to stop and photograph along the way.

items.activity: Arrive in Nan, check in to town accommodation
items.note: Stay in town tonight -- you will want to walk to the temples and evening market.

items.activity: Kad Khwuang Mueang Nan evening market (Fri-Sun)
items.note: Set in front of Wat Phumin -- people sit on woven trays eating northern food along the street. Very relaxed vibe.

blocks.text: Day 3 -- Nan City, Then Up to Pua-Bo Kluea

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Wat Phumin -- Pua -- Bo Kluea -- Stay in Sapan

items.activity: Wat Phumin + Nan National Museum
items.note: Wat Phumin is over 400 years old -- go for the murals, especially the famous whispering couple (Pu Man and Ya Man). Nearby, the museum building itself is a photogenic spot with frangipani archways.

items.activity: Drive up to Pua
items.note: About 1 hour from Nan town. A small market town set in paddy fields -- noticeably cooler than the city.

items.activity: Rong Bom Pua cafe (converted tobacco curing barn)
items.note: A cafe built inside an old tobacco drying barn, with views over the terraced rice fields. A good coffee stop before the mountain drive.

items.activity: Drive up to Bo Kluea via Doi Phu Kha
items.note: The road winds beautifully -- stop at Doi Phu Kha viewpoint and Bend No. 3 along the way. Drive slowly and watch the corners.

items.activity: Bo Kluea mountain salt wells
items.note: Ancient salt brine springs in a mountain valley where locals still boil salt the traditional way. You can buy spa-grade salt as a souvenir.

items.activity: Enter Sapan village, check in
items.note: A small village by a stream in a mountain valley. Lots of bamboo homestays. Morning fog rolls in most mornings.

items.activity: Dinner in the village, listen to the stream
items.note: There are only a few restaurants in Sapan and they close early -- eat before dark.

blocks.html: This is the most driving-heavy day, but also the most rewarding. You get Nan's cultural side in the morning and its mountain landscape in the afternoon. The Pua-Bo Kluea-Sapan stretch is what people come back for -- partly because waking up to valley fog is exactly as good as it looks in photos, and partly because the drive back down in the dark is not fun. Staying overnight in Sapan is the comfortable choice.

blocks.title: Booking Sapan Accommodation
blocks.html: Homestays and view rooms in Sapan and Bo Kluea sell out fast in cool season (Nov-Jan). If you are timing the trip for morning fog, book weeks ahead -- riverside rooms and mountain-view rooms go first.

blocks.text: Day 4 -- Morning Fog, Then Head Home

blocks.label: Day 4
blocks.title: Catch the Morning Fog -- Streamside Cafe -- Drive Home

items.activity: Watch the morning fog in Sapan
items.note: The village viewpoint or the bridge over the Nam Wa river. Fog typically rolls through in the early hours before the sun rises.

items.activity: Breakfast, pack up
items.note: Most homestays include breakfast.

items.activity: Stop at a streamside cafe on the way down
items.note: The Bo Kluea-Sapan road has a few cafes beside clear streams -- worth a sit-down before the long drive.

items.activity: Drive back down to Nan city or head south toward Phrae
items.note: If you are flying, head to Nan Nakhon Airport. If you drove up from Bangkok, run Highway 101 back through Phrae.

items.activity: Pick up souvenirs before leaving
items.note: From Nan: mountain coffee, woven fabrics, Bo Kluea spa salt. From Phrae: indigo cloth and khao khaep rice crackers.

blocks.html: No need to pack the last day with activities -- the mountain descent takes time and focus. Take in the morning fog, have a slow coffee by the water, then ease your way back. If you drove up from Bangkok, budget for another long stretch of driving in the afternoon: Nan and Phrae to the capital is still several hours away.

blocks.text: Adjust the Plan to Your Time

items.name: Only 3 Days / 2 Nights
items.blurb: Trim Phrae old town to half a day and push straight up to Nan. Focus on Wat Phumin, Pua, Bo Kluea, and one night in Sapan.

items.name: Want to Go Slower
items.blurb: Stretch to 5 days -- two nights in Phrae to really cover the cafes and old town, then move up to Nan without rushing.

items.name: Fog Season Trip
items.blurb: Nov-Jan brings the coolest air and the best morning fog around Sapan and Bo Kluea. Peak season, though -- book accommodation well in advance.

items: Accommodation -- Phrae town guesthouses ~600-1,200 THB/night · Sapan/Bo Kluea homestays ~800-2,000 THB/room depending on the view
Food -- Northern Thai local meals run ~50-120 THB · Cafe drinks ~60-110 THB
Petrol + tolls -- Driving from Bangkok return, budget a few thousand THB for fuel depending on your car
Entry fees -- Baan Wongburi and the national museum are a few tens of baht each · most temples are free

faq.q: How long does it take to drive from Phrae to Nan?
faq.a: From Phrae town centre to Nan town centre on Highway 101 is about 118 km -- roughly 2 hours. The road is in good condition, with some winding sections near the end as you approach Nan.

faq.q: How many days do you need for Phrae and Nan?
faq.a: Four days and three nights is the sweet spot: a day and a half in Phrae old town, then two days in Nan covering Wat Phumin in the city and the Pua-Bo Kluea-Sapan mountain area. Three days works if you cut Phrae short.

faq.q: What is the best time of year to visit Phrae and Nan?
faq.a: November to January is the coolest month range and when morning fog blankets the valleys around Sapan and Bo Kluea -- visually the best time. It is also peak season, so accommodation fills up fast and needs booking ahead. Rainy season (June-October) turns the rice paddies brilliant green but mountain roads get slippery.

faq.q: Do I need to rent a car?
faq.a: Yes, strongly recommended. Many of Nan's highlights -- especially Pua, Bo Kluea, and Sapan -- are outside town and have no convenient public transport. If you would rather not drive the full distance from Bangkok, fly into Nan Nakhon Airport and rent a car there to cover both provinces.

faq.q: Are Sapan and Bo Kluea far from Nan city?
faq.a: Yes, it is a full mountain drive. Nan to Pua is about 1 hour, then another 1.5-2 hours on winding mountain road through Doi Phu Kha to reach Bo Kluea and Sapan. Most people overnight in Sapan rather than attempting a day trip.
